Octopuses have three hearts… and blue blood.
Two hearts pump blood through the gills, to pick up oxygen. The third pumps it to the rest of the body.
And here's the weird part: that third heart stops beating when the octopus swims. That's why they'd rather crawl.
Their blood is blue because it carries oxygen with copper, not iron like ours.
Copper works better in cold water with little oxygen, deep in the ocean.
And two thirds of an octopus's brain cells are in its arms. Each arm can touch, taste and react on its own.
